chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who pledged an item that had produce/yield, that its yield is accounted for the owner of the pledge from what is owed to him.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (a title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.رَهْن: Pledge or guarantee (a financial contract where an item is held as security for a debt)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الرَّهْنِ: The pledgee, the person holding the item as security
key_terms.غَلَّة: Yield, produce, or fruit generated by the pledged item

ai.seo_question: Who is entitled to the yield or produce of a pledged item in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him), recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes the principle that the yield (ghallah) of a pledged asset accrues to the pledgee to offset the debt, reflecting the pre-Islamic and early Islamic commercial practice of *ribah* (usury/interest) which was later refined. It highlights the practical application of justice in financial transactions, ensuring the creditor benefits from the asset's productivity while the debtor is relieved of an equivalent portion of the principal. This precedent underscores the dynamic nature of Shia jurisprudence in adapting commercial laws to ensure equity between parties.
